Subject: Draft redlines on SLA + suggested maintenance phasing (see attachments)

Jordan / Britech procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, attached are two artifacts: a marked Order Form with the SLA redlines we discussed (Redlines_OrderForm_v2.docx) and a simple Maintenance Phase Table that maps planned maintenance windows to impact buckets (Maintenance_Phase_Table.xlsx). Key highlights we added based on your ask: 

- Uptime buckets: we propose an availability measurement on a rolling 30-day window (vs calendar month) to better align with your traffic variability.
- Service credits: tiered credits tied to severity-based incidents (P1/P2) but capped at a quarterly maximum — we added examples in the doc.
- Response vs. Resolution: we separated initial response (acknowledgement) from remediation time. Response windows remain short (15 / 60 min for P1/P2) while remediation targets are objective-driven and dependent on root cause.
- Maintenance phasing: recommended classification (routine, phased, disruptive) with advance notice windows and optional blackout dates for your major launches.

Action items I propose: 
1) Jordan: please confirm whether rolling 30-day measurement is acceptable to your Ops team.
2) Procurement/legal: flag any non-starters on credits caps or notification timing.
3) Lauren / Marissa / Neha (cc): can you review the draft redlines for exposure on reserved capacity and fallbacks?

If helpful, we can schedule a short call next week to walk through the phase table and the examples for credits.

Cheers,

--
Priyom Das

Priyom —

Thanks for sending these over. High-level reactions from Legal & Ops after a quick review: 

- Rolling 30-day measurement: ops is open but legal prefers calendar month for auditability. Can you provide rationale/metrics for why rolling 30 better reflects load?
- Credits cap: our standard practice is no artificial quarterly cap for availability credits; instead we prefer an annual cap tied to total fees. Would Redwood accept an annual cap at X% of annual fees?
- Maintenance windows: the phased approach looks promising; however, we need guaranteed blackout windows for our fiscal quarter-end (we'll call these "locked weeks"). Can Redwood commit to no disruptive maintenance during locked weeks with at least 14 days notice for phased work?
- Incident definition: please clarify whether degraded performance (e.g., 20% increased latency) qualifies as a P2 or is only P3. We need clearer thresholds in the Order Form.

We'll attach our tracked changes back after procurement confirms the rolling measurement point. Also copying Jordan from Applications for the Ops perspective.

Thanks,

Claire Redwood

Jordan / Claire / team —

Thanks for the quick review and the clear asks. After an internal sync (Ops + Legal + Sales), here is a concise compromise we can take to Britech for an operational sign-off: 

1) Measurement window: we'll accept calendar-month measurement in the Order Form but will add language that allows us to report a rolling 30-day view for operational dashboards. Purpose: auditable month for contract terms; rolling window for debugging and trending.

2) Service credits cap: propose an annual cap at 6% of annualized fees (instead of an uncapped or quarterly cap). If uptime falls below 95% for two consecutive months, we'll trigger an expedited remediation plan with increased credits for the subsequent month (details in redline).

3) Incident thresholds: we propose explicit thresholds in the Order Form — P1 = total unavailability for >5 consecutive minutes affecting majority of API endpoints; P2 = ≥30% latency degradation sustained for >20 minutes; P3 = partial degradation or single-region impacts. We'll translate these into precise measurement queries and include examples.

4) Maintenance phasing & blackout weeks: Redwood can commit to respecting two locked weeks per quarter designated by Britech with no disruptive maintenance. For phased maintenance we will provide a minimum 14-day notice; for routine non-disruptive updates we will provide 72 hours notice. We will include an optional emergency maintenance clause with immediate notification and a follow-up postmortem.

Next steps: if this high-level compromise is acceptable, can Britech confirm the two locked weeks they want reserved (we'll accept provisional weeks and we can finalize on the call)? Also, Lauren / Marissa / Neha — please review the proposed credit % and the incident definitions for any legal/ops exposure we should modify before the call.

If useful I can send an updated Redlines_OrderForm_v3 with tracked changes after we align internally. 

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to jump on a 30-min sync with Jordan + Claire to finalize.

Best,
